【保養須知】每年至少調音1-2次。環境溫度20-25度，濕度40-60%。琴鍵用: [Care] Have the piano tuned at least once or twice a year. Keep the room at 20–25 °C and 40–60 % humidity. Wipe the keys with a soft, slightly damp cloth. Keep the piano out of direct sunlight and do not put things on top of it. In humid regions use a dehumidifying rod or a dehumidifier. Every two to three years have the instrument fully regulated, including lubricating the action and reshaping the hammers.
【基本指法與技巧】C大調音階右手：12312345，左手：54321321。五指: [Basic fingering and technique] C major scale, right hand: 12312345; left hand: 54321321. Five-finger position exercise: put the thumb on middle C and the other fingers in order on D, E, F and G; lift and lower each finger while the others stay put. Passing the thumb under the other fingers and crossing the other fingers over the thumb are the basic motions behind scales and arpeggios. Hanon exercises for 10-15 minutes a day train finger independence. Studies such as Chopin's and Liszt's études train technique and musicianship together.
【基本演奏姿勢】坐於琴椅前半部，背部挺直。距離鍵盤以手肘呈90度為標準。雙腳平放: [Basic sitting position] Sit on the front half of the bench with your back straight. The distance to the keyboard is right when the elbows are at 90 degrees. Both feet flat on the floor, the right foot in front of the right pedal. Fingers curved as if holding a ball, playing with the fingertips. The wrist is level with the forearm, the hand keeps its arch, and the shoulders stay relaxed. The fingers are numbered: thumb (1), index (2), middle (3), ring (4), little finger (5). Good posture is the foundation of every technique and directly affects comfort and progress.
【經典曲目】初級階段：貝多芬《給愛麗絲》、巴哈《小步舞曲》、貝多芬《月光奏鳴曲》: [Classic repertoire] Beginner stage: Beethoven's Für Elise, Bach's Minuet, the first movement of Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata, Chopin's Nocturne in E-flat major. Intermediate stage: Chopin's Revolutionary Étude, Debussy's Clair de lune, the third of Liszt's Liebesträume, a Rachmaninoff Prelude. Advanced stage: Liszt's Hungarian Rhapsody No. 2, Chopin's Scherzo No. 1, Rachmaninoff's Piano Concerto No. 3, Prokofiev's Sonata No. 7.
【練習方法與建議】每日練習建議分配：哈農10分鐘、音階琶音15分鐘、練習曲15分: [Practice routine and advice] A suggested daily split: Hanon 10 minutes, scales and arpeggios 15 minutes, studies 15 minutes, pieces 20 minutes. Effective practice habits: (1) slow practice — keep the tempo within what you can fully control; (2) hands separate — learn each hand until it is secure, then put them together; (3) short sections — break the piece into small passages and take them one at a time; (4) metronome — build a steady sense of rhythm; (5) memorising — learn the piece in sections and understand its structure. Common study books: Beyer, Czerny, Hanon, Bach's Inventions, Chopin's études, Liszt's études.
【著名鋼琴家】古典：李斯特、蕭邦、克拉拉·舒曼。二十世紀：霍洛維茲、魯賓斯坦、顧: [Famous pianists] Classical: Liszt, Chopin, Clara Schumann. Twentieth century: Horowitz, Rubinstein, Gould, Argerich. Contemporary: Lang Lang, Yuja Wang, Zimerman, Trifonov. Every pianist has a distinctive style; listening to many different players' recordings helps you build your own musical taste.
【踏板運用】右踏板（延音踏板）：最常用，踩下後所有音延長，在和聲變換時更換。左踏: [Using the pedals] Right pedal (sustain): the most used — pressing it lengthens every note, and it is changed at each change of harmony. Left pedal (soft): the action shifts to the left, so the volume drops and the timbre softens. Middle pedal (sostenuto): sustains only the notes sounding when it is pressed, for passages that need particular notes to keep ringing. The pedal is a major means of expression in piano playing and needs practice of its own.
【鋼琴的歷史】鋼琴起源於1709年，義大利人克里斯多佛利發明了第一台可以控制強弱: [The history of the piano] The piano began in 1709, when the Italian Cristofori built the first keyboard instrument that could control loud and soft, naming it the pianoforte (soft-loud). The harpsichords before it could only produce a fixed volume and could not shade dynamics. In the later eighteenth century the Viennese piano was favoured by Mozart and Haydn. In the early nineteenth century Beethoven's piano music demanded a wider dynamic range, which drove innovation in piano making. In the 1820s the Frenchman Érard invented the double escapement, letting a key repeat quickly and laying the foundation for the brilliant technique of the Romantic era. Steinway & Sons was founded in 1853 and is still a byword for the finest pianos. The piano moved from European aristocratic salons out to the public and became the most popular of instruments.
【鋼琴結構與類型】平台鋼琴（三角鋼琴）：琴弦水平放置，音量大、反應靈敏，是音樂廳: [Structure and types] Grand piano: the strings lie horizontally; the sound is large and the response quick — the first choice for a concert hall. Upright piano: the strings stand vertically, saving space and costing less, which suits the home. A piano has about 12,000 parts: 88 keys (52 white, 36 black), the action, hammers (wooden cores covered in felt), 220 strings (three per note in the treble, two in the middle, one copper-wound string in the bass), the soundboard (which turns vibration into sound), the cast-iron frame (which bears 20 tonnes of tension), and three pedals.

Felt hammers strike the strings, and the vibration passes through the bridge to the soundboard, which amplifies it; most notes use three strings, and the bass runs from one string up to two. A modern piano has 88 keys, is tuned to the equal-tempered chromatic scale, and has a wide range with a bright, clear tone. Volume is controlled by the pressure on the key: the harder the press, the stronger the strike and the louder the sound. The right pedal lifts the dampers, so notes ring on and can overlap. Compared with the harpsichord, the piano can change dynamics continuously according to touch; compared with the clavichord, the hammer leaves the string at once, so the sound is louder and can be sustained.

The piano is a keyboard chordophone that developed in Europe / Italy, Hornbostel–Sachs number 314.122-4-8. The player presses a key, which drives a small felt-covered wooden hammer to strike a steel string; the vibration passes through the bridge to the soundboard, which amplifies it, and a damper stops the string when the key is released. Most modern pianos have 88 black and white keys, are tuned to the equal-tempered chromatic scale, and come in grand and upright forms. It is used in classical, jazz, traditional and popular music for solos, chamber music, accompaniment, composition, songwriting and rehearsal, and is also common in schools, venues and rehearsal rooms.
鋼琴源自歐洲鍵盤與擊弦樂器傳統。中世紀有管風琴與來自中東的擊弦揚琴；17世紀小鍵: The piano grew out of the European keyboard and struck-string tradition. The Middle Ages had the pipe organ and the struck-string dulcimer from the Middle East; in the seventeenth century the mechanisms of the clavichord and the harpsichord reached maturity. Around 1700 Cristofori, in Italy, built a keyboard instrument that struck the strings with hammers and responded to the strength of the touch, its name taken from the harpsichord with soft and loud. In 1711 Maffei's article spread the method of building it, Silbermann added the forerunner of the sustain pedal, and Bach approved of it in 1747. In the later eighteenth century the Viennese and English actions separated, and the grand and the upright gradually became the mainstream; in the nineteenth century, under the influence of Romantic music, the cast-iron frame and the divided string choirs raised tension, volume and sustain, and the modern 88-key layout became general.
鋼琴發聲部件以木製槌外包絨氈敲擊鋼絲弦，弦振經橋碼傳至音板；現代琴鍵為黑白相間。: The sounding parts of the piano are a wooden hammer covered in felt that strikes steel strings, with the string vibration passing through the bridge to the soundboard; the keys of a modern piano alternate black and white. Nineteenth-century pianos used a cast-iron frame to bear greater string tension. Early Viennese pianos used a wooden frame, two strings per note and hammers covered in leather, and on some the black and white keys were reversed. Cristofori named one of his keyboard instruments after cypress wood, but the sources do not state the material of the case, soundboard, bracing and other remaining parts.
鋼琴的聆聽場合以古典音樂為主，亦見於爵士、傳統與流行音樂，常作獨奏、重奏、伴奏與: You mostly hear the piano in classical music, but also in jazz, traditional and popular music: as a solo instrument, in chamber music, as accompaniment and in a band, and in composition and rehearsal. Grand pianos are mostly used for concerts; uprights, being smaller and cheaper, are common in homes, schools and rehearsal rooms. The literature offers Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 29, Chopin's Winter Wind Étude, Liszt's Transcendental Études, Balakirev's Islamey, Stravinsky's Petrushka and Ravel's Gaspard de la nuit, showing its wide range, variable dynamics and power to carry harmony forward.
